### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. atrial septal defect 3  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.717)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:7576)

**Proposed mechanism:** MYH6 (HGNC:7576) —DISRUPTS→ Cardiac muscle development and function (GO:0060047); Cardiac muscle development and function (GO:0060047) —LEADS_TO→ Atrial septal defect (HP:0001684); Cardiac muscle development and function (GO:0060047) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy (HP:0001638). Mutations in MYH6 lead to haploinsufficiency, disrupting normal cardiac muscle development and function, which in turn causes both atrial septal defects and cardiomyopathies.

**How to falsify it:** The hypothesis would be falsified if pathogenic variants in MYH6 were found to be exclusively associated with one disease and absent in the other, or if different functional consequences (e.g., LoF for one and GoF for the other) were definitively established for each disease. _(variant: Exclusion of common pathogenic variants in MYH6 (e.g., allele frequency >0.1% in gnomAD) from individuals with either disease would weaken the shared causal gene hypothesis.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis of these cardiac conditions can facilitate the development of targeted therapies and improved diagnostic strategies for patients with MYH6-related heart diseases. Focusing on MYH6 function could lead to interventions benefiting patients with either atrial septal defect 3 or MYH6-related cardiomyopathies.

#### 2. dilated cardiomyopathy 1EE  —  Tier 2 — Strong / Probable  (fitness 0.698)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:7576)

**Proposed mechanism:** MYH6 (HGNC:7576) —DISRUPTS→ Cardiac muscle development and function (GO:0060046); Cardiac muscle development and function (GO:0060046) —LEADS_TO→ Atrial septal defect (HP:0001631); Cardiac muscle development and function (GO:0060046) —LEADS_TO→ Dilated cardiomyopathy (HP:0001635). Haploinsufficiency of MYH6 disrupts normal cardiac muscle development and function, leading to the distinct but overlapping phenotypes of atrial septal defects and dilated cardiomyopathy.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in MYH6 that exhibit gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects, rather than haploinsufficiency, for either disease would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: gnomAD v2.1.1 data showing a pathogenic variant with >1% allele frequency in the population.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis of these cardiac conditions in MYH6 can inform diagnostic strategies and potentially lead to targeted therapeutic interventions for patients with related disorders.

#### 3. hypertrophic cardiomyopathy 8  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.419)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-390522)

**Proposed mechanism:** MYH6 (HGNC:7487) —DISRUPTS→ Cardiac muscle contraction (GO:0060046); MYL3 (HGNC:7501) —DISRUPTS→ Cardiac muscle contraction (GO:0060046); Cardiac muscle contraction (GO:0060046) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy (HP:0001638); Cardiac muscle contraction (GO:0060046) —LEADS_TO→ Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HP:0001645). Mutations in MYH6 and MYL3 disrupt the cardiac muscle contraction pathway, leading to both general cardiomyopathy and specifically hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in MYH6 or MYL3 that do not segregate with either disease phenotype in affected families, or finding a significant burden of such variants in unaffected individuals in gnomAD. _(variant: HGMD-associated variants in MYH6 or MYL3 with AF > 0.01)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of MYH6 and MYL3 in cardiac muscle contraction provides a common therapeutic target for both diseases, potentially enabling the development of drugs that restore normal sarcomere function.

#### 4. lethal congenital contracture syndrome 4  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.417)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-390522)

**Proposed mechanism:** MYH6 (HGNC:7487) —DISRUPTS→ Cardiac muscle contraction (GO:0060044); Cardiac muscle contraction (GO:0060044) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital heart defect (HP:0001627); Cardiac muscle contraction (GO:0060044) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy (HP:0011674); MYBPC1 (HGNC:7506) —DISRUPTS→ Skeletal muscle contraction (GO:0003010); Skeletal muscle contraction (GO:0003010) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital contracture (HP:0002672); Skeletal muscle contraction (GO:0003010) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital lethal contracture syndrome 4 (MONDO:0013965). Haploinsufficiency of MYH6 disrupts cardiac muscle contraction, leading to congenital heart defects and cardiomyopathy. Similarly, haploinsufficiency of MYBPC1 disrupts skeletal muscle contraction, resulting in congenital contractures and lethal congenital contracture syndrome 4. Both diseases converge on the fundamental processes of muscle contraction, albeit in different muscle types.

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of pathogenic variants in MYH6 or MYBPC1, respectively, that are present at a high frequency (e.g., >0.1%) in general population databases like gnomAD would cast doubt on their primary causal role in these rare diseases. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on fundamental muscle contraction machinery for both conditions could pave the way for therapeutic strategies that target common downstream pathways or molecular chaperones involved in myofibril assembly and function, potentially benefiting patients with either disease.

**Proposed mechanism:** MYH6 (HGNC:7492) —DISRUPTS→ Sarcomere structure and function (GO:0030016); Sarcomere structure and function (GO:0030016) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital heart defect (HP:0001627); MYBPC1 (HGNC:7500) —DISRUPTS→ Sarcomere structure and function (GO:0030016); Sarcomere structure and function (GO:0030016) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital myopathy (HP:0003198); Congenital myopathy (HP:0003198) —LEADS_TO→ Tremor (HP:0001311). Mutations in MYH6 disrupt sarcomere structure and function, leading to congenital heart defects. Similarly, mutations in MYBPC1 disrupt sarcomere structure and function, leading to congenital myopathy, which can include tremor.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies reveal that MYH6 mutations exclusively affect cardiac tissue and MYBPC1 mutations exclusively affect skeletal muscle, with no overlap in downstream cellular processes or pathways, this hypothesis would be falsified. Furthermore, if variants in MYH6 or MYBPC1 are found at a significant frequency (>1%) in general population databases like gnomAD and are not enriched in affected individuals, it would challenge their causal role. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of sarcomere integrity in both cardiac and skeletal muscle diseases could lead to therapeutic strategies that target common downstream pathways or structural components, potentially benefiting patients with either condition. For instance, therapies aimed at stabilizing sarcomeric proteins could be explored.

#### 7. arthrogryposis multiplex congenita 6  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.382)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-390522)

**Proposed mechanism:** Loss-of-function variant in NEB (null) —DISRUPTS→ NEB (HGNC:7745); NEB (HGNC:7745) —DISRUPTS→ Nebulin function in sarcomere assembly and stability (null); Nebulin function in sarcomere assembly and stability (null) —DECREASES→ Sarcomere integrity and function (null); Sarcomere integrity and function (null) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle hypotonia (HP:0001252); Loss-of-function variant in MYH6 (null) —DISRUPTS→ MYH6 (HGNC:7504); MYH6 (HGNC:7504) —DISRUPTS→ Myosin-6 function in muscle contraction (null); Myosin-6 function in muscle contraction (null) —DECREASES→ Sarcomere integrity and function (null); Sarcomere integrity and function (null) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital myopathy (HP:0003198). Loss-of-function variants in NEB disrupt its role in sarcomere assembly and stability, leading to muscle hypotonia (Disease A). Similarly, loss-of-function variants in MYH6 impair myosin-6 function in muscle contraction, compromising sarcomere integrity and leading to congenital myopathy (Disease B). Both NEB and MYH6 contribute to the overall integrity and function of the sarcomere, a shared pathway whose disruption underlies both conditions.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in NEB or MYH6 in individuals with the respective diseases that are present at a high frequency (>1%) in gnomAD, or if the functional studies demonstrate gain-of-function mechanisms for both diseases. _(variant: null)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of NEB and MYH6 in sarcomere integrity provides a potential therapeutic target for both diseases. Modulating pathways that support sarcomere stability or compensate for the loss of these proteins could offer a unified treatment strategy.

**Why it matters:** Identifying the shared mechanistic link through sarcomere organization could pave the way for therapeutic strategies that target common downstream pathways to ameliorate muscle dysfunction in both conditions.
